chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a kur of food on him, so he bought a kur from another man, and he said to the man, 'Go and take full measure of your kur.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.اسْتَوْفِ: Take full measure; to complete the measurement accurately.
key_terms.كُرٌّ: A unit of volume or weight used in trade, often referring to a specific measure of grain or food.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it; a common juristic phrase indicating permissibility.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy food by measuring it from what is already in your possession?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of selling a specific quantity of food (*kur*) already in the buyer's possession, a key issue in the chapter on *Bay' al-Madmun* (sale of guaranteed/possessed goods). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the transaction by allowing the buyer to direct the seller to measure the exact amount, establishing that physical separation or precise measurement suffices to transfer ownership without requiring prior full possession by the seller. This ruling underscores the flexibility in commercial transactions within Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the clarity of the commodity's quantity and quality over rigid possession timelines.
